question: The recent death of Mahmoud Bakhum, a street vendor in Seville who, panicked by a police chase, fell into the River Guadalquivir, shows just how serious reports of racial bias in police action are. A number of reports drawn up by Spain’s ombudsman and human rights organisations document continuing practices, such as racial profiling, which perpetuate discrimination and breach fundamental rights.

What is more, it is apparent that there are barriers to properly reporting such practices and resistance within institutions to acknowledging the problem. Is the Commission considering proposing an EU mechanism to monitor, collect data and act in cases of institutional racism in security forces?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.4.2025) The Commission condemns any form of violence. Violence runs counter to the common values upon which the EU is built. As the Commission set out in its reply to written questions E-003732/2020, E-005750/2020, enforcement authorities should always be exercised in a proportionate manner. Inhumane or degrading treatment of any individual is unacceptable.

Maintenance of law and order is primarily a competence of the Member States. They must promote and ensure respect of fundamental rights as provided for in their constitutional order and under their international law commitments.

In the case referred to by the Honourable Member, it is therefore for the Spanish authorities to conduct independent and accountable investigations leading to the determination of all relevant facts, in accordance with national legislation and international human rights obligations.
